blocking.section: Decision outcome (State Store failure row; Figure 1)
blocking.issue: The State Store failure row lists fewer `RZ-STS` cases than the registry in Scalability and distributed state. That registry also has RZ-STS-004, for a call that is never attempted because the per-request deadline was spent or the in-flight ceiling was full (pack section 8.7 rule 2: "remaining Policies apply `failureMode` without waiting"). A `ratelimit` Policy with `failureMode: closed` placed after a slow Policy gets 503 `RZ-STS-004`. The ADR's rule does not cover this trigger, and its code range leaves the code out. This regression came from my earlier non-blocking suggestion to write "RZ-STS-001 to RZ-STS-003", which also missed RZ-STS-004.
blocking.evidence: Line 54: "A failed or timed-out call, or an open State client breaker, applies `failureMode`: ... `closed` returns 503 `RZ-STS-001` to `RZ-STS-003`". Line 80: "fm -- \"closed\" --> r503[\"503 RZ-STS-001 to RZ-STS-003\"]". Compare docs/architecture/11-scalability-and-distributed-state.md, State client and RZ-STS error codes: "| RZ-STS-004 | Per pack 8.10 | Not attempted: the per-request deadline was spent or the in-flight ceiling full |", and the same section: "at most 8,192 blocking calls in flight (target) ... an excess call is skipped under `failureMode`".
blocking.fix: In line 54, change "A failed or timed-out call, or an open State client breaker," to "A failed, timed-out or unattempted call, or an open State client breaker," (+1 word). Change "`RZ-STS-001` to `RZ-STS-003`" to "`RZ-STS-001` to `RZ-STS-004`". In Figure 1, relabel r503 as "503 RZ-STS-001 to RZ-STS-004" and the edge `gcra -- "error, timeout or NOSCRIPT"` as "error, timeout, NOSCRIPT or not attempted". Fenced text is not counted toward the length band.

blocking.issue: The ADR and its owning document give different refill rules for fail-open buckets. The ADR refills them once per aligned window. The owning document refills them in 60 steps once the window is longer than 1 minute. With a `1h` limit, the ADR lets a key spend a whole hourly ceiling in the first second of each hour, and twice within seconds across an hour boundary. The owning document spreads that ceiling across the hour. This wording came from the fix for L2-3 and L1-1, so it is a regression. L1-5 reports the same problem.
blocking.evidence: Line 54: "`open` (default) admits from the local buckets, which then refill once per epoch-aligned `window` without carry-over". Compare docs/architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md, Per-Node ceiling: "each derived-ceiling bucket holds max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published) tokens per epoch-aligned window, without carry-over, refilled in 60 steps past 1 minute (target)".
blocking.fix: In line 54, replace "which then refill once per epoch-aligned `window` without carry-over" with "which then refill per epoch-aligned `window`, in 60 steps past 1 minute, without carry-over" (+4 words). Keep the More information clause "aligned-window fail-open refill for declared ceilings too"; it already records the extension to declared ceilings as a pending amendment.

blocking.issue: The ADR's per-key bound on State Store calls is twice the bound in its owning document and in Scalability and distributed state. The ADR's figure is arithmetically correct: a full bucket plus one window's refill is 2 × ceiling per Node. However, the ADR lists only the Library catalog wording as a correction, so readers cannot tell which bound to trust. It also leaves the Failure matrix row "Hot constant key saturates a shard: Up to N × ceiling calls per window" uncorrected. The change came from the fix for L1-1, so it is a regression. L1-5 reports the same problem.
blocking.evidence: Line 85: "- Good, because a key reaches the State Store at most min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling) times per window (target), a bucket's capacity plus its refill". Line 139: "- Tech stack correction: the Library catalog's \"`NOSCRIPT` fallback\" means the `failureMode` path above, never an `EVAL` retry." Compare docs/architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md, Decision path: "A key reaches the State Store at most min(offered, N × ceiling) times per window." Compare docs/architecture/11-scalability-and-distributed-state.md, Hot keys: "A key reaches the State Store at most min(offered, N_serving × ceiling) times per window".
blocking.fix: Replace line 139 with: "- Corrections: the Library catalog's \"`NOSCRIPT` fallback\" means the `failureMode` path above, never an `EVAL` retry; Traffic management's and Scalability's N × ceiling call bound is 2 × N × ceiling." This adds 10 words. To stay within the 1,500-word maximum, delete ", as pack sections 7 and 8.8 fix" from the Chosen option sentence on line 43 (−7 words). That phrase resolved no earlier finding, and the Fail-open bound row already states the pack section 8.8 bound. With L2-5 and L2-6 applied, the body goes from 1,489 to about 1,497 words.

non_blocking.suggestion: Style guide section 4 wants a tag on the same line as every scale figure. The owning document tags the clamp "max(1, `requests` / 100) (target)", but line 54 carries no tag. Add "(target)" after the clamp (+1 word).

The bullet lists OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 as a pack section 8.8 amendment. Its recommended option (c), a persisted Node count, amends pack section 8.11, as OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 says ("packs 8.8 and 8.11"). Change "Pending pack section 8.8 amendments" to "Pending pack sections 8.8 and 8.11 amendments" (+2 words). With L2-5 to L2-7 and the tag above, the body reaches exactly 1,500 words.

non_blocking.section: Decision outcome (GCRA row) versus pack section 7
non_blocking.suggestion: Pack section 7 and pack section 8.8 say "single Lua EVAL". The ADR says "one `EVALSHA`", which matches the owning document. EVALSHA is the cached form of EVAL, so this is not a contradiction. Still, record it as a pack section 7 wording correction, either in the Corrections bullet or in the foundation amendments below, so later readers do not take it for a deviation.

No file in docs/_meta/research/ records that rueidis `Lua.Exec` retries with `EVAL` on `NOSCRIPT`. The cited URL is only the repository root. Add a research row with the source file URL, so the ban on `Lua.Exec` rests on recorded evidence.

foundation_amendments: Pack section 7 Rate limiting row and pack section 8.8: replace "single Lua EVAL" with "one `EVALSHA` per Policy; `NOSCRIPT` applies `failureMode` and schedules a single-flight reload, never an `EVAL` retry" (pack section 8.7 rule 1).

Pack section 8.8: while State Store calls fail, local buckets refill per epoch-aligned window without carry-over, in 60 steps past 1 minute, for declared and derived ceilings alike, so the N × per-Node ceiling fail-open bound holds per window.

Traffic management and resilience (Decision path, Failure matrix hot-key row) and Scalability and distributed state (Hot keys): the per-key State Store call bound is min(offered, 2 × N × ceiling) per window, a bucket's capacity plus its refill, not N × ceiling.
